front: What does the abbreviation PLC stand for?
excerpt: A programmable logic controller (PLC) or programmable controller is an industrial computer that has been ruggedized
mnemonic: You Program its Logic, and it Controls the machine: Programmable Logic Controller.

front: What is a programmable logic controller (PLC)?
back: A ruggedized industrial computer adapted to control manufacturing processes such as assembly lines, machines and robotic devices.
excerpt: an industrial computer that has been ruggedized and adapted for the control of manufacturing processes, such as assembly lines, machines, robotic devices

back: An electrically operated switch: control signals on its input terminals operate its contacts.
excerpt: A relay is an electrically operated switch. It has a set of input terminals for one or more control signals, and a set of operating contact terminals.

front: What does a relay let an independent low-power signal do?
excerpt: Relays are used to control a circuit by an independent low-power signal

front: Which logic function do relay contacts wired in series perform?
back: Logical AND: current passes only if all the contacts are closed.
excerpt: Just as a series of relay contacts performs a logical AND function, not allowing current to pass unless all the contacts are closed
mnemonic: Series = a chain: one open link and nothing gets through, so contact 1 AND contact 2 AND contact 3 must all be closed.

front: Why was it difficult to change the control logic of a hard-wired relay system?
back: The logic was fixed in the wiring, so a change required rewiring and careful updating of the documentation.
excerpt: The hard-wired nature of these components made it difficult for design engineers to alter the automation process. Changes would require rewiring and careful updating of the documentation.

front: A relay system is reconfigured by changing hardware. How is a PLC reconfigured instead?
back: By loading new or modified code into it; no hardware changes are needed.
excerpt: While relay systems required tedious and sometimes complicated hardware changes in case of reconfiguration, a PLC can be reconfigured by loading new or modified code.

front: What operating-system drawback do desktop computers have as industrial controllers compared with PLCs?
back: Desktop computers run on less stable operating systems than PLCs.
excerpt: desktop computers run on less stable operating systems than PLCs

front: Why is a PLC classed as a hard real-time system?
back: Its outputs must be produced in response to input conditions within a limited time, so that unintended operations do not result.
excerpt: A PLC is an example of a hard real-time system: output results must be produced in response to input conditions within a limited time, so that unintended operations do not result.

front: In a modular PLC, what does the chassis (rack) provide?
back: Space for modules chosen for the application: power supply, processor, input/output modules and communication interfaces.
excerpt: has a chassis (also called a rack) that provides space for modules with different functions, such as power supply, processor, selection of I/O modules and communication interfaces

front: What does remote input/output (I/O), such as an external rack of I/O modules, do to a PLC system's response time?
back: It introduces additional uncertainty into the response time.
excerpt: that introduces additional uncertainty in the response time of the PLC system.

front: What is a human-machine interface (HMI) used for in a PLC system?
back: It lets people interact with the controller for configuration, alarm reporting or everyday control.
excerpt: PLCs may need to interact with people for the purpose of configuration, alarm reporting, or everyday control. A human-machine interface (HMI) is employed for this purpose.
